subject: Seasonal buffer + consumption-floor tradeoffs for 2027 renewal
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@everestanalytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity outlook and renewal options for Q4 spike

Hi Logan,

Quick note — our usage for Q4 last year hit a 3x week-over-week spike around Black Friday, and procurement wants to understand options earlier for our July 2027 renewal. We ran the numbers and want to avoid overcommitting but also need predictable availability during seasonal peaks.

Two approaches procurement asked to compare:
- A small consumption floor (minimum committed consumption) with lower unit rates when exceeded
- A voucher-style buffer (prepaid buffer units that burn first) with rollover capped to one quarter

Can you and the team sketch pricing tradeoffs and any SLA or priority routing guarantees for the buffer? Also, we have a legal window — they need a quote + summary to start the PO process by Apr 9.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Cloud Ops, Everest Analytics
attachments: scenario_matrix_v1.xlsx (see referenced)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity outlook and renewal options for Q4 spike

Hi Alicia — thanks for the context and the urgency. High-level thoughts before we do the math:

- Consumption floor: predictable baseline pricing, simpler invoicing, but risk of paying for unused units if you miss the spike by a narrow margin. Good if spikes are repeatable and you want commitment discounts.
- Voucher buffer: prepay for a burst pool that routes preferentially during capacity contention; better for one-off seasonal bursts and avoids long-term overcommitment, but careful with rollover and unit economics.

I’ve looped in Marcus (pricing lead) and Ben (sales ops) to model a side-by-side comparison. Marcus — can you produce a two-scenario matrix (floor at 25% of avg monthly consumption w/ 15% discount vs voucher 2M tokens buffer w/ 6-month rollover) and call out expected per-token spend across projected spike profiles?

We’ll aim to get a firm quote and SLA addendum by Apr 8 to give procurement time to start the PO. If procurement needs a template PO line, we can attach one.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: EVR-4127 — model inputs for seasonal buffer vs floor

Team — thread for the Everest quote. Alicia needs a side-by-side by EOD Apr 7. Key inputs:

- Baseline (avg month): 150M tokens
- Peak week during season: +300M tokens (3x)
- Renewal term: 12 months co-term with existing January cycle (they want a July mid-contract change)

2) Voucher buffer option: prepaid 6M tokens buffer per month for 3 months (burn-first), voucher price at list-5% with single-quarter rollover cap

Also include: estimated unit cost across three spike profiles (mild/medium/extreme), routing priority delta (what we guarantee for voucher buffer), and the incremental SLA addendum wording (we can offer a 99.5% burst availability target with documented failover to hosted fallback). I attached scenario_matrix_v2.xlsx with placeholders — please update.

Irene — legal will want the short SLA addendum. Can you draft a 1-paragraph addon we can share with procurement?

Thx — Logan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: EVR-4127 — model inputs for seasonal buffer vs floor

Quick drop-in: I updated scenario_matrix_v2.xlsx with the three spike profiles and ran the blended unit-costs. Short summary:

- Consumption floor (40M/mo at 18%): lowers expected annual unit cost by ~11% under medium-repeat spikes, but produces ~6% wasted cost if spikes do not materialize.
- Voucher buffer (6M/mo x3 months @ list-5%): reduces peak-week marginal cost by ~22% compared to on-demand routing during contention and carries zero baseline waste in non-spike months, but offers less gross discount if spikes are sustained for longer than 3 months.

Routing/priority note: voucher buffers are eligible for fast-path routing when our preferred machines are saturated; we can commit to a burst availability target (99.5%) in the addendum. Fallback behavior: if buffer exhausted, requests fall back to their pinned model at standard priority.

I attached the updated matrix. Recommend we present both options and include a recommended hybrid: smaller floor (20M) + voucher buffer (3M x3) to hedge.

— Marcus
(attachment: scenario_matrix_v2.xlsx)
